title: How Rivers Build New Land
objective: After this level you can explain how floodplains and deltas form where a river slows down and drops its load.
summary: Slowing floodwater drops coarse grains as levees and fine silt across the floodplain. At its mouth a river builds a delta; cut off its sediment, as on the Nile, and the delta shrinks.

cards.headline: Some of the world's richest farmland was delivered by floods.
cards.body: Ancient Egypt grew up on the Nile's floodplain. The same rivers that carry land away upstream build new land downstream. The whole trick is slowing down.

cards.headline: A flood's delivery
cards.body: Level 23 ended with a rule: slow water drops its load. A flood puts it to work. When a river overtops its banks and spreads across its floodplain, the flat land beside it, the water slows sharply. The coarsest grains drop first, right beside the channel, building low ridges called natural levees. Finer silt and clay settle farther out. Flood after flood, that nutrient-rich silt makes floodplains very fertile farmland.

cards.headline: Building at the mouth
cards.body: The biggest slowdown comes at a river's mouth. The current fades, the sediment falls to the bottom, and a delta grows. As it builds out, the river splits into smaller branching channels called distributaries. The name comes from the triangle-shaped Greek letter delta (Δ), the shape of the Nile's delta. Not every delta keeps that shape: the Mississippi builds a bird's-foot.

cards.context: A delta grows only while sediment keeps arriving. On the Nile, the Aswan High Dam and other river management now hold back the sediment that once reached the coast, and the coast is eroding. Cut the supply and the land retreats.

cards.headline: New land: built
learned: Floods slow on the floodplain and drop their load
Deltas grow where rivers slow at their mouths
Cut off the sediment and a delta shrinks

questions.prompt: The smaller channels that branch off a river across its delta are called _____.

options.label: meanders
options.rationale: Meanders are bends in a river.

options.label: levees
options.rationale: Levees are ridges along the banks.

options.label: oxbows
options.rationale: Oxbows are abandoned loops that became lakes.

questions.explanation: As a delta builds out, the river splits into smaller branching channels called distributaries.

questions.prompt: Match each river feature with what it is.
questions.explanation: A floodplain is the flat land beside a river, natural levees are low ridges by the channel, and distributaries are the smaller branching channels of a delta.

questions.prompt: Fine silt and clay settle across a floodplain, then get buried and compacted. Using Level 6, which rock can they become?

options.label: Granite
options.rationale: Granite is igneous, cooled from magma.

options.label: Marble
options.rationale: Marble is metamorphic, made from limestone.

questions.explanation: Shale is the fine-grained sedimentary rock made of silt- and clay-sized particles.
